assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset for a rich handcrafted pixel-art historical industrial adventure game. Match the reference's warm amber furnace lighting, soot-dark brick, plain riveted iron and readable mechanical silhouettes. Crisp detailed pixel clusters, no smooth painting, no photorealism, no HUD, titles, labels, borders, arrows, diagrams, people or hands. Single full-frame 16:9 landscape; exact scene composition for draggable objects drawn later by the game. Opaque background. Create a new CLOSE-UP EMPTY heavy oak-and-iron workbench inside the approved mechanized foundry. Slightly elevated front view, matching panels one and five in reference, but without ANY loose puzzle objects. Thick worn dark golden oak tabletop stretches full width from x=5% to95%, and from y=36% to90%, abundant usable top surface in center. Brick factory wall, shaft and belts, restrained glowing furnace to far upper left, small factory window in upper background. Wood bench front and two stout iron-braced legs below. A few fixed tools hang on the wall only; tiny crates at extreme edges are fine. Center tabletop is EMPTY, no bars, rod, templates, file, tongs, caliper, ruler, objects or people anywhere on tabletop. No giant central fireplace. This empty bench will serve choosing billets, filing/fit and a small transmission test rig; preserve clean readable central area.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production TRANSPARENT sprite atlas for the approved pixel-art ironworking puzzle. EXACT regular grid of FOUR columns and THREE rows: 12 isolated objects, one centered entirely INSIDE each equally sized cell, generous transparent margin between ALL cells. All sprites viewed in coherent slightly raised front workshop perspective, rich crisp pixel clusters and dark outlines, warm amber highlights. No background, cast floor shadows, text, numbers, frame, grid lines, extra objects or hands. Keep every sprite wholly within its cell. Row 1 left-to-right: (0) short thick rectangular iron billet; (1) medium-length thick wrought iron billet, clearly distinct correct size; (2) very long thin iron billet; (3) rough solid elongated connecting-rod forging blank with thick SOLID ends, no holes. Row 2 left-to-right: (4) partly forged solid connecting-rod blank, slim central neck and two thick SOLID circular ends, no holes; (5) clean fully forged connecting-rod blank with SMALL solid circular left end and LARGER solid circular right end, NO HOLES yet; (6) finished gray iron connecting rod, SMALL circular left eye and LARGER circular right eye, both with clear transparent drilled holes, horizontal and nearly symmetrical center axis; (7) wooden matching template board with the connecting-rod silhouette cut into it, two eye positions. Row 3 left-to-right: (8) long rough steel hand file with short wooden handle, horizontal; (9) a long iron pair of forging tongs with wooden handles, horizontal; (10) wood billet-length reference gauge with a recess matching billet 1; (11) brass-and-iron workshop caliper. The two eye centers on connecting rod sprites should be about 12% and88% of the tightly cropped object width, consistent across states. All metal is COLD GRAY, runtime will tint hot blanks; no glow haze. Genuinely transparent background.
